f3e4879ac88cc5d1.title: Coforge Q2 results: Net profit surges 56.5% to ₹588 cr, revenue up 53.6%
f3e4879ac88cc5d1.summary: Coforge posted a 56.5 per cent increase in consolidated profit to Rs 588 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by AI-led execution of deals, the company said on Friday. The IT firm had posted a net profit of Rs 375.8 crore in the same period a year ago. "Right now the margin uptake that we are seeing is in the existing fixed price projects where AI is getting infused," Coforge Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Sudhir Singh, said during the company's earnings call. Coforge signed 8 large deals the highest number signed in a single quarter across North America, Europe and Australia, which led to a total contract value of the new orders of USD 1.04 billion during the reported quarter. The company increased the operational profit margin guidance to 17 per cent for the next year from the range of 15.5 per cent to 16 per cent. Revenue from operations during the reported quarter increased by 53.6 per cent to Rs 6,171 crore from Rs 4,016 crore a year

The shooting took place at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, about 180 kilometres (110 miles) south of the capital, Amman. Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed two gunmen who appear to be holding pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man who appears to be holding a semiautomatic rifle then approaches and opens fire, and all three then run toward the church. Video footage taken by witnesses shows broken glass and pools of blood on the floor of the church. Dorgham Halasa, who was among the mourners inside the church, said intense gunfire erupted 15 minutes after the funeral had started, and then people started running. "It was a weird situation, and heavy gunfire," Halasa said. He did not see the gunmen, but said other people reported seeing four of them. The Associated Press could not independently verify the number

b8b8014b8ecf7b27.title: Aung San Suu Kyi speaks to son after five years in detention in Myanmar
b8b8014b8ecf7b27.summary: The son of Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi said Friday that when he finally got to speak with his mother, who has spent more than five years in detention in the Southeast Asian country, it seemed in some ways like not much time had passed at all. "She sounds like herself, and still sounds strong," said Kim Aris, adding that her voice was a bit croaky, like she had a cold. Myanmar's military government on Thursday allowed Aris a 20-minute phone call with his 81-year-old mother, one of the world's most famous political prisoners. He spoke from Myanmar's embassy in London to Suu Kyi in her country's capital, Naypyitaw, where she's serving an 18-year sentence under house arrest. Suu Kyi has been detained since February 2021, when Myanmar's army ousted her elected government. Held mostly incommunicado, she's serving an 18-year prison term on charges that supporters and rights groups say are bogus and politically inspired. It's not the first time she has been kept as a prisoner -

2759c8ffd56e2f7a.title: Rescuers search for survivors after Tibet earthquake kills 16, injures 76
2759c8ffd56e2f7a.summary: Rescuers combed through a remote area in the Chinese region of Tibet on Friday after a magnitude 7 earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured 76 and collapsed hundreds of homes, according to Chinese state media. The disaster struck Nagqu, a city north of Tibet's capital Lhasa that is some 4,800 metres (15,748 feet) above sea level, on Thursday. At least 339 homes collapsed, and officials told journalists they were concerned about further building collapses from aftershocks, as well as casualties from rockslides. China's national broadcaster CCTV aired footage on Friday showing collapsed houses and shattered stone walls in Nagqu. More than 12,000 residents in the region were evacuated, with additional shelters under construction, China's official news agency Xinhua reported. No one was reported missing in Baqen County in Nagqu, where the earthquake struck. Search and rescue efforts are complicated by the geography and low temperatures, officials said. 1b57d91edcfdc6bd.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22.5% to ₹4,993 cr as fuel price freeze hits earnings
1b57d91edcfdc6bd.summary: State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs. BPCL's standalone net profit declined to Rs 4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from Rs 6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore from Rs 10,968 crore. India's second largest fuel retailer earned USD 32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to USD 10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back. 1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.title: Ashoke Sen becomes first Indian physicist to win 2026 Oskar Klein Medal
1ca9ef8d9f92f32d.summary: Indian physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first Indian physicist to receive the honour. Sen, an ICTS-Infosys Madhava Chair professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS)-Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), Bengaluru, is widely regarded as an architect of modern string theory. The theory postulates that the elementary constituents of matter are tiny one-dimensional, string-like objects instead of point particles. It thus tries to put forth a unifying description for matter and forces between them. Established in 1988 and named after the Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein, the medal is awarded annually by Stockholm University and the Nobel Committee for Physics of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. Honouring the memory of Klein, the organising committee of the Oskar Klein Memorial Lectures every year invites a distinguished researcher to give a memorial lecture and to receive the Klein medal. 2c154bb19c3f4ee2.title: 5.3-magnitude earthquake hits China's Qinghai days after Tibet quake
2c154bb19c3f4ee2.summary: A 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck China's Qinghai province on Saturday, two days after a powerful 7.0-magnitude temblor in neighbouring Tibet left 16 people dead and 76 others injured. The latest quake jolted Zadoi County in northwest China's Qinghai Province at 4:39 pm (Beijing Time), according to the China Earthquake Networks Centre (CENC). The epicentre, at a depth of 10 kilometres, was monitored at 32.54 degrees north latitude and 93.97 degrees east longitude, the centre said. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage from Saturday's earthquake. The fragile Tibetan Plateau is prone to powerful earthquakes as it lies in a region where the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates collide, generating significant seismic activity. Published - October 24, 2026 08:31 pm IST - HUBBALLI The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The special drive against use of manja launched by the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissionerate continued on Saturday with more cases being booked taking the total number of cases booked to 16. A day after a 38-year old woman was killed after manja (abrasive kite string) slit her throat in Hubballi, the Police Commissionerate had launched the special drive on Friday. According to the Hubballi Dharwad Police Commissioner, during the special drive, 124 places were inspected and 69 locations where manja was being used were checked. The police had so far removed dangerously hanging manja strings at 63 locations and checked 67 shops where manja was being reportedly sold. While 11 cases including those against sellers, users, and also a parent for allowing a kid to use the abrasive string to fly kite were booked on Friday, five more cases were booked in Bendigeri, Old Hubballi, APMC Navanagar, and Kasabapet police stations on Saturday. On Thursday, lab technician Vidya Manjunath Goudar was killed after the abrasive kite string got entangled around her neck, slitting her throat, while she was riding a two-wheeler. The incident led to backlash and various leaders, including Pralhad Joshi, Basavaraj Horatti, Prasad Abbayya and others, calling for strict action against the sale and use of manja. Published - October 24, 2026 08:33 pm IST - PUDUCHERRY Chief Electoral Officer A.S.P.S. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Chief Electoral Officer A.S.P.S. Ravi Prakash held a meeting with representatives of six recognised political parties in Puducherry to brief them on the Special Summary Revision (SSR) exercise being undertaken in the Union Territory. The Election Commission of India has directed the Election Department to undertake the SSR of the photo electoral roll in the Union Territory. The representatives of political parties were informed about the procedural aspects involved in the conduct of the SSR. The instructions given by the ECI were passed on to the representatives of political parties at the meeting held on Friday. The CEO sought the cooperation of all parties in ensuring the smooth conduct of the revision process, a release here said. “During the meeting, the CEO explained the important legal provisions and procedural aspects of the SSR, with particular emphasis on the instructions given by the Election Commission. The CEO also clarified and addressed the concerns raised by the representatives of political parties,” the release said. Deputy Chief Electoral officers B. Thillaivel and M. Kandasamy were present. 555d80f878d4d30a.title: Anniversary of Mysore Chalo observed in city
555d80f878d4d30a.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:28 pm IST - MYSURU The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram The Mysuru District and City Freedom Fighters’ Association commemorated the 80th anniversary of the Mysore Chalo movement at the Freedom Fighters’ Park in Subbarayana Kere on Saturday. Members of the Freedom Fighters’ Association garlanded the statue of Mahatma Gandhi at 10.30 a.m. They later took out a march to Ramaswamy Circle and paid a floral tribute at the memorial of Ramaswamy, who sacrificed his life on September 13, 1947, for the freedom of Mysuru. The Mysore Chalo movement, which began on September 1, 1947, played a significant role in the freedom of the Princely State of Mysuru. While India attained Independence on August 15, 1947, Mysuru hoisted the national flag for the first time on October 24, 1947, marking the beginning of the Independence era. While speaking on the occasion, Yogananda, Working president of the Freedom Fighters’ Association, said, “On October 24, 1947, Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, the then ruler of the Mysuru State, announced the merger of the Princely State into the Indian Union and declared Independence.” Association Secretary Ravi, Pandith Aradya and others were present on the occasion. Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST - SIVAGANGA RAMANATHAPURAM: TAMIL NADU: 24 October 2026: Tamil Nadu Ministers paying floral tributes at Maruthu Pandiyar brothers memorial in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. Photo: handout_e_mail / The Hindu. | Photo Credit: HANDOUT_E_MAIL Marking the 225th death anniversary of Maruthu Pandiyar brothers, leaders from various political parties garlanded the statues at the manimandapam in Tirupattur in Sivaganga district on Saturday. The memorial day of the Maruthu Pandiyar brothers was observed as a government event at the manimandapam in Tirupattur, Sivaganga district. District Collector P. Akash hoisted the national flag and garlanded the statues of the Maruthu brothers. District Superintendent of Police Abhishek Gupta, District Revenue Officer Sailendran, and others participated. Minister for Energy Resources and Law C. T. R. Nirmal Kumar, Minister for Natural Resources T. K. Prabhu, Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and Minister for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises P. Mathan Raja, paid their respects at the venue. On behalf of DMK, former ministers K. R. Periyakaruppan, R. S. Rajakannappan, T. R. B. Rajaa, MLA Muthuraja, former MLA Tamilarasi, and Town Panchayat President Sengaimaran paid their respects. On behalf of AIADMK, former ministers Dindigul C. Srinivasan, Sellur K. Raju, Gokula Indira, Kamaraj, Manikandan, and former MLAs Rajan Chellappa and Senthilnathan paid their respects. MDMK General Secretary Vaiko, AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran, BJP District Secretary Pandithurai, Congress National Secretary Mayura Jayakumar, former MLAs Mangudi, among others paid their respects. CPI(M) District Secretary Mohan, Communist Party of India former MLA Gunasekaran, also paid their respects. Published - October 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST

Published - October 24, 2026 08:27 pm IST - TIRUNELVELI Tirunelveli district monitoring officer Sandeep Nanduri inspects the drainage desilting work in Tirunelveli Town on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Tirunelveli district monitoring officer Sandeep Nanduri reviewed the precautionary measures taken in the district to tackle the Northeast monsoon in the presence of Collector Anand Mohan on Saturday. During the the review meeting, Mr. Nanduri said that with the onset of monsoon and widespread rainfall in the district, the district administration has taken immediate precautionary measures to tackle the situation of heavy rain and flooding. He added that areas vulnerable to heavy rains had been identified and were being closely monitored, with necessary precautionary measures in place. More than 5,466 volunteers are ready to assist in rescue operations, he noted. Mr. Nanduri further said that seven relief centres had been kept ready to provide safe shelter to people in the event of heavy rain. Similarly, buildings such as schools and marriage halls had also been identified and kept ready to set up as relief centres, depending on the situation. He stressed that essential facilities including drinking water, medical facilities, food and generators are available to the public in these centres without any hindrance. He also emphasised the need to create awareness among farmers about precautionary measures to protect crops from damage caused by heavy rains. In case of crop damage due to disaster situations, the concerned officials should be prepared to immediately assess the damage and take appropriate measures to provide relief to affected farmers, Mr. Nanduri said. Aroma Chundan crossed the finish line in 3 minutes and 21.227 seconds to win the title. Melpadam Chundan, rowed by Pallathuruthy Boat Club, finished second in 3 minutes and 21.802 seconds, followed by Niranam Chundan of Niranam Boat Club in 3 minutes and 21.925 seconds. Veeyapuram, Cheruthana, Arppookara, Punyalan Niranam, Nadubhagam and Thalavady finished fourth to ninth, respectively. In the smaller boat categories, Puthenparambil won in the Iruttukuthi B-grade event, Champion clinched the Veppu B-grade title, Moozhi won in the Churulan category and Munnuthaikkal emerged victorious in the Iruttukuthi A-grade event. Aroma Boat Club will receive ₹5 lakh in prize money for the victory, while Pallathuruthy Boat Club and Niranam Boat Club will receive ₹3 lakh and ₹1 lakh, respectively, for finishing second and third. District Police Chief K.M. Sabu Mathew distributed the prizes at the valedictory function. 64bedd84a350a66a.title: Four-year-old boy from Tiruppur district dies of dengue
64bedd84a350a66a.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:27 pm IST - COIMBATORE The Health Department has confirmed the death of a four-year-old boy from Tiruppur district due to dengue. The child, identified as Tamil from Kungumapalayam village in Palladam Block, was diagnosed with Dengue Shock Syndrome combined with sepsis and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC), at the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital, where he was referred to by a private clinic. In a press release, Hospital Dean M. Geethanjali said that since the child was admitted with after-effects of two epileptic attacks and low blood-pressure, normal saline bolus, and noradrenaline adrenaline were administered. There was respiratory failure and the child was kept in life-support. Though attempts were made to normalise blood pressure, the child suffered circulatory failure, and despite administering blood products and resuscitative efforts, the child died of cardiac arrest on Friday night, the press release said. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:41 pm IST - TIRUVARUR: Compensation under the the Prime Minister’s crop insurance scheme has been released to farmers who were not able to take up sowing during the kuruvai season in 2026-27 in Tiruvarur district. According to an official release, the Centre has announced that a sum of ₹77.70 crore would be distributed as compensation to farmers in 159 hamlets in Tiruvarur district under the ‘prevented sowing’ clause of the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY). While a sum of ₹12.05 crore would be disbursed to 4,868 farmers in the first phase on October 24, it would be distributed to others in subsequent phases. The amount would be credited directly into the accounts of the beneficiaries. Kuruvai coverage in Tiruvarur district stood at 77,573 hectares last year and dropped by 31,235 hectares this year, the release added. Murali, former Principal of The Madura College, who spoke on ‘Changing directions of Higher Education in Tamil Nadu,’ warned that Tamil Nadu’s higher education sector was facing several crises, and the government appeared to be facilitating the expansion of private and foreign universities instead of strengthening public universities and government colleges. Asserting that education is not merely a means of obtaining employment, he described it as a vital public resource that fosters independent thinking, scientific temper, social justice, human rights awareness, and democratic values. He cautioned that the growing tendency to transform education into a commercial service directly threatens the educational rights of students from poor and middle-class backgrounds. Periasamy A TNSTC bus driver was killed when the vehicle he was driving came in the path of a landslide at Burliyar, near the Coimbatore-Nilgiris district border, on the intervening night of Friday (October 23, 2026) and Saturday (October 24). There were no other passengers in the bus; the conductor, who sustained injuries, has been admitted to a hospital. According to the rainfall report issued by the Nilgiris district administration, Burliyar recorded 250 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending at 7 a.m. on Saturday, which was categorised as extremely heavy rainfall. More than 300 people were stranded along the ghat section following multiple landslips. A TNSTC bus plying on the Coimbatore-Nilgiris route was struck by a landslip at Burliyar in the early hours of Saturday, with soil and debris falling onto the vehicle. Photo & video: M. Periasamy (@peri_periasamy) https://t.co/3LKRVvMAtf The deceased driver was identified as Janagaraj, 55, of Katteri in the Nilgiris district. He was driving the bus from Coonoor to Coimbatore when the incident occurred. The conductor, Keshavan, was rescued and admitted to the Mettupalayam Government Hospital for treatment. A mini goods carrier also fell into a gorge at the landslip site. Its driver, Moushin, 38, managed to climb out of the vehicle and reach safety. He was admitted to the Coonoor Government Hospital for treatment . Updated - October 24, 2026 08:40 pm IST Preetham R is one of the youngest to be exhibiting his collection. Three years ago, Preetham R stumbled upon a small box stacked with coins in the almirah and fell in love with it. “Although my father had shown me his collection when I was much younger, it was in college that I took a liking to coins,” says the 22-year-old who completed his B.Com. He is one of the youngest who is participating in the three-day coin exhibition conducted by Chennai Coin Club that concludes on October 25. More than 50 numismatics from different states are taking part in this event, and Preetham’s short journey with coins shows that it is never too late to start a hobby. “I started segregating the coins in the box into different types and researching them to develop more interest,” says the resident of Ayanavaram. A one-rupee copper coin was one of his first that he brought home on his own. Today, the youngster has a collection of 1,000 coins, with those minted from 1950 onwards being his specialisation. At the ongoing exhibition, besides selling some of his coins, he hopes to buy some rare ones to add to his collection. For those keen on starting coin collection as a hobby now, he says, it is not just a knowledgeable and a learning experience but a good investment option. Organisers of the Chennai Coin Club exhibition say the three-day event is aimed at raising awareness about counterfeit currency and fake coins that are increasingly doing the rounds. All the participants at the exhibition are experienced numismatics who are showcasing their best collection and share their knowledge. Besides antique coins, historical banknotes and vintage stamps will be showcased. The event will serve as a platform to buy, sell and exchange currencies and coins. Published - October 24, 2026 08:55 pm IST - MYSURU Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile Mysuru royal family speaking to reporters in Mysuru on Saturday. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru has said she will issue a statement shortly on the circumstances that led to the cancellation of the traditional Vajra Mushti Kalaga during the Vijayadashami celebrations at the Mysuru palace on Wednesday. Responding to reporters’ queries in Mysuru, Ms. Wadiyar said she was yet to gather complete information about the developments that led to the cancellation of the historic martial tradition. Vajra Mushti Kalaga, an ancient form of martial combat in which wrestlers strike each other on their shaved heads with knuckle-dusters, has traditionally been held ahead of the erstwhile royal family’s private procession on Vijayadashami. The event was, however, cancelled this year after wrestlers alleged that the police had prevented some of them from entering the Mysuru palace premises in time to participate. Meanwhile, Ms. Wadiyar, however, expressed satisfaction over elephant Prashanta successfully carrying the golden howdah and ensuring the smooth completion of the Jamboo Savari. She admitted that she had been anxious about Prashanta carrying the golden howdah. It may be mentioned that it was 54-year-old male elephant Prashanta’s first time performing the task following the retirement of his predecessor, Abhimanyu, upon attaining the age of 60. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:52 pm IST - TIRUCHI The condition of several roads in Tiruchi has turned from bad to worse after the recent spell of rain. | Photo Credit: M. MOORTHY The wet spell over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the Northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been receiving rainfall. The showers were light until Thursday. However, heavy rain lashed different parts of the city on Friday, and the incessant rainfall has left arterial roads and interior lanes damaged. Uneven road surface and potholes have become a common sight on major stretches, with the top layer eroded at many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. The roads in Anna Nagar, Karur bypass, Old Madurai Road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around Central Bus Stand such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road have suffered significant deterioration. Similarly, stretches around Chathiram Bus Stand have also been damaged. Similar issues have cropped up around Gandhi Market, Palakarai, Varaganeri and other areas. With movement of heavy vehicles continuing through the roads, the loose surface material has begun to dislodge, worsening driving conditions. Recently patched up roads too have suffered damage. Motorists say the situation has grown increasingly unsafe, especially during the night. “We encounter many deep potholes and eroded stretches on the roads. They test the patience of motorists. We need to navigate carefully,” says R. Thiruvengadam, a social activist. Published - October 24, 2026 08:39 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Vaisakh Chandran. | Photo Credit: File Photo The last two seasons were forgettable for off-spinner Vaisakh Chandran. A finger injury, followed by a shoulder injury, sidelined him. In between, he lost his bowling action and, consequently, his wicket-taking ability. The Ranji Trophy match against Karnataka at the KCA Stadium in Mangalapuram last season was particularly chastening; he was savaged by Karun Nair and R. Smaran, conceding over 100 runs at nearly five runs an over. His shoulder injury then flared up, forcing him to spend the rest of the season in rehabilitation. “I knew something was wrong but I was helpless. I was just going through the motions in the match against Karnataka. The shoulder was hurting as well. I felt a sharp pain on my right shoulder whenever I threw the ball while fielding. I think I over-bowled in the nets. I was told to bowl 30 overs daily during practice by our former coach and I followed it. The pain worsened, forcing me to consult a doctor who advised rest,” During his rehabilitation, he watched the video of the Karnataka match and compared them with old footage and realised his bowling action had changed drastically. “I went back to the drawing board, worked on my action. I also sought the help of Biju George, who pointed out the flaws and helped me to correct them,” he said. “It is a common problem for all bowlers to lose their original action when they play a lot. Every bowler has a specific arm slot from which he delivers the ball comfortably. In Vaisakh’s case his release point and arm path were different from his earlier action. I made slight adjustments to his loading and recoil and things fell into place,” Biju.explained. Published - October 24, 2026 08:55 pm IST - HYDERABAD The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) detected violations at 125 medical shops across Hyderabad, its surrounding areas and other districts of Telangana during a special enforcement drive against the illegal sale and diversion of habit-forming drugs | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) detected violations at 125 medical shops across the State during a special enforcement drive against the illegal sale and diversion of habit-forming drugs. Show-cause notices have been issued to all 125 medical shops as discrepancies were detected. The Drugs Wing of TG SAFE, along with Enforcement Wing police personnel and Excise Enforcement personnel, conducted raids on Saturday (October 24), in areas covering Gajularamaram, Quthbullapur, Malkajgiri, Kapra, Habsiguda, Uppal, Jeedimetla, Balanagar, Medipally and Shamirpet. Similar enforcement operations were carried out in other districts of the State. The inspections focused on the indiscriminate sale of habit-forming medicines, including Tramadol, Alprazolam, Nitrazepam, Tapentadol, Zolpidem and Pregabalin-containing formulations, as well as codeine-containing cough syrups. TG SAFE officials conducted decoy operations and test purchases to check whether medical shops were dispensing prescription medicines, particularly those classified under Schedule H1 and Schedule X of the Drugs Rules, without complying with regulatory requirements. The violations detected included the sale of prescription medicines without valid prescriptions issued by registered medical practitioners, failure to maintain prescription and Schedule H1 drug registers, and dispensing medicines in the absence of a registered pharmacist. Updated - October 24, 2026 09:05 pm IST - HYDERABAD BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao at the inauguration RandomTrees office in Hyderabad. | Photo Credit: Arrangement BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao has urged youth to embrace Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an opportunity for innovation and employment, instead of living in fear of the technology, particularly its impact on jobs. The former IT and Industries Minister, who was inaugurating the India headquarters of data, AI and innovation firm RandomTrees here, said this underscoring the significance of continuous learning, skill development and harnessing emerging technologies. Every technological revolution initially creates apprehensions but eventually opens new avenues for growth, he said, recalling the resistance to introduction of computers in the banking sector. Adapting to change was essential for progress and portraying AI as a ‘monster’ would only create unnecessary fear among people, Mr. Rao said. Highlighting the importance of strengthening Telangana’s technology ecosystem, attracting investments and preparing youth for future employment opportunities, he said the BRS government had taken several initiatives to position Hyderabad as a leading global IT destination and attract global capability centres of multinational companies. He expressed confidence that the city could emerge as a major hub for AI research, data science and technological innovation, a release from his office on Saturday said. With private sector playing a major role in employment generation, the governments should focus on creating a business-friendly environment rather than attempting to provide jobs directly to everyone. Reliable power and water supply, quality infrastructure, efficient transport and ease of doing business were essential to attract investments, Mr. Rao said. Published - October

4223785a7993584b.title: Bhatti Vikramarka calls for judicious use of water, electricity amid El Nino concerns
4223785a7993584b.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - KHAMMAM Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Saturday called for collective efforts to conserve water and electricity amid dry weather conditions and rising power demand, urging the Opposition parties to set aside political differences to tackle the emerging El Nino-related challenges. . Addressing the media at Kodumuru in Chintakani mandal of Khammam district, he appealed to the Opposition to rise above political differences, recalling the collective efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy had reviewed the situation and constituted a Cabinet Sub-Committee to address the challenges, he said. Mr. Vikramarka said peak power demand had risen from 6,648 MW at the time of Telangana’s formation in 2014 to 20,018 MW now. Daily electricity consumption had increased from 245.35 million units in October last year to 335.05 million units this October, a rise of about 37%. He said the expansion of transmission infrastructure and construction of new substations were helping the State manage the growing demand. However, declining reservoir levels were affecting hydropower generation, which normally supplies around 3,500 MW during peak night-time hours. Of the nearly three million agricultural pump sets in the State, around 1.5 million were reportedly facing groundwater shortages. He urged farmers in areas with inadequate groundwater to avoid operating motors to prevent damage to pumps and transformers. The State’s major reservoirs, with a combined capacity of 470.22 TMC, held only 178.60 TMC of water, while nearly 40% of its 44,034 tanks had less than one-fourth of their capacity filled. Mr. Vikramarka said the government would prioritise water conservation while protecting livelihoods of farmers, labourers and rural communities. Published - October 24, 2026 09:0

Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST As in the previous year, Amirda Varshini, councillor, Ward 126, has initiated a slew of measures to reassure residents that her team would be available to attend to any monsoon-related issue. This time, she has launched a helpline number (8010000126) and a QR code for people in Ward 126 to report any issue. “This service is available all through the day during the monsoon time,” she says, adding that water logging, electricity-related complaints and tree fall are among the top grievances they get. Talking to The Hindu Downtown, she says that barring a few areas where storm water drain work is yet to be commissioned many other localities are ready to face the monsoon. Mandavelipakkam, parts of Mandaveli, Devanathan Street, Jeth Nagar, Trustpakkam, and fishing hamlets such as Pattanipakkam and Rajiv Gandhi Nagar are among areas that fall under Ward 126. “My big focus will be on the coastal regions as many of the houses are old and they really need help,” says Amirda. Published - October 24, 2026 08:56 pm IST - PALAKKAD The Palakkad chapter of the Victims Information, Sensitisation, Welfare and Assistance Society (VISWAS) India will conduct a district-level children’s parliament competition for Class XI and XII students here on November 9. The event will be held in association with the State Bank of India (SBI) as part of the State government’s anti-drug campaign Operation Toofan. The competition will focus on drug use among students. Schools must conduct preliminary rounds and nominate the first prize winner for the district-level final. Students can choose from six topics covering drug prevention, awareness, youth responsibility and the need to protect students from substance abuse. Schools must email the details of their winning students to viswaspkd.programs@gmail.com before November 3, 2026. The final will be held at the Collectorate conference hall at Civil Station here. District Collector Sudheer K. will preside over the function. MLAs and senior police and excise officials will attend. Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen will be the chief guest. The first, second and third-place winners will receive mementoes and certificates. Five students will receive consolation prizes, and all participants will get certificates. For details, contact P. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government have come under sustained attack from the Iran-backed Houthis, shifting the focus of the wider West Asia war that erupted with U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. 5880547296026a16.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 09:10 pm IST - COIMBATORE The parents and relatives of Akilan, a Class 11 student of a government-aided school in Peelamedu who had ended his life due to alleged harassment over caste and eating habits, staged a sit-in protest demanding the arrest of his teacher, headmaster and other students purportedly involved in abetment. They refused to accept the body of the student. The Peelamedu police had registered a case against the teacher and a few classmates based on a complaint lodged by the deceased student’s mother Kausalyadevi. Two students were arrested after the case was registered. A press release issued by the city police said two students have been arrested in the case, and 30 other students, teachers and other witnesses were questioned. Separate inquiries were also conducted by officials of School Education Department and Child Welfare Committee. The autopsy report will provide more clues. Five special teams have been formed and CCTV camera footage and scientific evidence were being examined. The press release said that a transparent investigation was under way and that spreading of rumours should be avoided. Updated - October 24, 2026 09:00 pm IST - AMALAPURAM The Konaseema Centre for Migration (KCM) is gearing up to launch a village-level campaign against fake recruitment agents and agencies in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema district to prevent locals from being stranded in the Gulf region. The local agents are allegedly active in recruiting people—mostly women—for employment in the Gulf region, where victims are reportedly subjected to physical harassment, assigned work beyond their physical capacities, and stranded without employment. KCM manager Golla Ramesh stated that 284 people stranded in the Gulf region had been repatriated and 128 grievances pertaining to fake agents and agencies are being redressed. In a review meeting with the officials concerned, District Revenue Officer Veerla Subbarao directed the revenue, police, and other officials to launch a campaign against fake agents and agencies and create awareness on the employment opportunities and recruitment procedures. In a review meeting with the officials concerned, District Revenue Officer Veerla Subbarao directed the revenue, police, and other officials to launch a campaign against fake agents and agencies and create awareness on the employment opportunities and recruitment procedures. Updated - October 24, 2026 09:03 pm IST The fifth edition of Tattva 2026, an inclusive art platform dedicated to celebrating the creativity, talent, and aspirations of artists with disabilities, will be inaugurated on October 28. Initiated by V-Excel Educational Trust, this year the festival brings together 270 plus artists from across Tamil Nadu and Kolkata for five immersive days of artistic expression, mentorship, and public engagement. This is being organised around five thematic pillars — Drishti, Srishti, Anubhav, Vistara, and Ekattva, serving as a catalyst for social inclusion, offering structured workshops, live demonstrations, collaborative murals, a curated art auction, and dedicated sales platforms designed to foster economic independence and livelihood opportunities for participating artists, said a release. In a release, Vasudha Prakash, Founder-Director of V-Excel Educational Trust, said: “This year, we also celebrate the success stories of past participants, reaffirming our core belief that talent flourishes when properly nurtured. Through exhibitions, live demonstrations, and our new art auction, Tattva 2026 connects extraordinary creators with wider audiences.” As part of this year’s celebrations, V-Excel Educational Trust will host a special art auction on October 25 at 5 p.m. at Hotel Savera. The auction will showcase selected artworks created by artists with disabilities, offering art enthusiasts and collectors an opportunity to engage with their work while supporting the artists and their creative journeys. a435a348810cc741.title: Forum urges CM to frame rules for Malayalam Language Act
a435a348810cc741.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 09:02 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram Eminent names from the cultural, literary, and other spheres in Keralam, under the umbrella of the Aikya Malayala Prasthanam, have urged Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to implement the Malayalam Language Act to coincide with the 70th anniversary of the State’s formation. In a representation, prominent figures such as Adoor Gopalakrishnan, George Onakkoor, V. Madhusoodhanan Nair, C. Radhakrishnan, K. Satchidanandan, M. Mukundan, and N.S. Madhavan have pointed out that though Keralam was formed in 1956 along linguistic lines with Malayalam as its language, it neither had a language policy nor planning. Malayalam was not seen as the foundation of the State’s development nor was it projected with pride. Governments too were responsible for the neglect of Malayalam. This should change. The Malayalam Language Bill that was passed by the State Assembly in October last year became an Act after the Governor gave his assent in March this year. However, only on implementation could the Act be said to have achieved its objective. Seven months after Malayalam was declared the official language of Kerala, the Act was yet to get Rules. This was a matter of concern. On Kerala Piravi day (November 1) this year, Rules for the Malayalam Language Act should be framed and the State government should declare that Act will be implemented effectively, the representation sought. Some of the other signatories include C.V. Balakrishnan, M.N. Karassery, V.N. Murali, K.N. Ganesh, Subhash Chandran, Ezhacherry Ramachandran, P.K. Rajasekharan, Ambikasuthan Mangad, R.V.G. Menon, Alankode Leelakrishnan, Kaleeswaram Raj and M.R. Thampan. 9243627e57fe77bd.title: CJP seeks impartial probe into Chorabagan stampede that killed 19 in Bengal
9243627e57fe77bd.summary: CJP's West Bengal unit on Saturday demanded an impartial probe into the Chorabagan stampede that claimed 19 lives and called for accountability for any negligence established during the investigation. The party organised a condolence programme and a press conference to pay tribute to the victims and express solidarity with the affected families. Addressing the press conference, a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) member called for safety audits, trained personnel, emergency evacuation plans and better coordination among emergency services. In a statement, CJP coordinator Prakriti Sahu outlined the party's demands, including timely financial assistance and medical support for the affected families and injured, stronger safety guidelines for major public gatherings and festival pandals across the state, and regular public updates on the investigation and relief measures. The party said it would submit its demands in writing to the relevant authorities and seek details of the action taken.

a30320a748957285.title: HYDRAA operation unearths illegal extraction of water from Sunnam Cheruvu
a30320a748957285.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:20 pm IST - HYDERABAD Pipelines dropped into Sunnam Cheruvu. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) has unearthed several establishments drawing water illegally from Sunnam Cheruvu, Madhapur. In a major operation on Saturday (October 24, 2026), HYDRAA forces removed dozens of pipelines discreetly laid into the lake from several buildings at Borabanda Phase-3 and Navbharat Nagar areas. The large hoses were attached to pump sets in the residential buildings on the other end, and buried under the earth outside to avoid detection. The houses raided revealed massive bore-wells drilled in bedrooms and kitchen areas, a statement from HYDRAA said. Photos and videos shared by the agency showed water sumps and bore-wells dug up beneath cots. Using heavy machinery, HYDRAA forces excavated the pipelines and traced them back to their source points. The operation which began at 6.30 a.m. continued up to evening, with officials removing 15 bore-wells, and unearthing a large number of pipes laid into the lakes. The statement said HYDRAA acted upon complaints from local residents about depleting ground water reserves due to unlawful extraction of water from the lake for supplying to hotels and hostels in Madhapur. Updated - October 24, 2026 08:07 pm IST - MYSURU The Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary | Photo Credit: File Photo A network of human rights organisations will conduct a fact-finding mission into the fatal shooting of three persons in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Hanur taluk of Chamarajanagar district that took place in the early hours of August 20. The two-day high-level fact-finding mission, scheduled for Monday and Tuesday, October 26 and 27, will be jointly led by former Solapur Commissioner Harish Mangalal Baijal, IPS, and retired Karnataka Forest Service officer Raju, a former IFS officer. Representatives of several human rights organisations will be part of the mission. In a press statement, People’s Watch executive director Henri Tiphagne said three farmers were killed, and another person was injured in the shooting involving Karnataka Forest Department personnel. Identifying the deceased as Anthony Sami, John Rose Peter and Kumar, alias Savariyappan, the statement said the fourth person, Mahimai Das, was reportedly injured and subsequently taken to a hospital. The Forest Department has reportedly maintained that the four men had illegally entered the forest to hunt wildlife and were carrying weapons. According to the department’s account, the men had attempted to fire at forest personnel, who returned fire in self-defence. However, family members of the deceased and others associated with them have disputed this account. They maintained that the men were farmers who entered the forest in connection with their livestock, not to hunt wildlife, the statement said. The incident, therefore, should not be viewed merely as a confrontation between forest personnel and alleged hunters, the statement said. Published - October 24, 2026 08:09 pm IST - Hyderabad Women lighting a lamp during the fourth Bathukamma & Dasara celebrations at Studio Center in Detroit, United States. The spirit of Telangana didn’t just travel to Michigan, it bloomed there. The Global Telangana Association (GTA) Detroit Chapter hosted its fourth Bathukamma & Dasara celebrations at the Studio Center with around 1,800 members of the Telugu diaspora gathering for a vibrant display of culture, devotion, and belonging. The venue transformed into a riot of colours as women and young girls arrived adorned in beautiful silk sarees and traditional langa vonis . But the true centerpiece was hundreds of intricately arranged Bathukamma flower mounds, brought by attendees as offerings to Goddess Gowri and mother nature. The air resonated with devotional songs as participants danced in circles around the floral stacks, their synchronized claps and movements creating a mesmerizing spectacle. The festivities opened on a spiritual note with a traditional Shami pooja conducted by the local temple priest. The GTA Detroit executive committee left no stone unturned in crafting a holistic community experience. A , specially prepared by local Indian restaurant Aha Biryani, was served to all the attendees. Prominent leaders from various Indian communities, including the Michigan Republican Party Treasurer, Sunny Reddy, graced the occasion. b5ae7ec62dcc2fd2.title: Farmers express happiness over continuous rainfall
b5ae7ec62dcc2fd2.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 08:09 pm IST - DINDIGUL Farmers in Dindigul district expressed their happiness over the continuous rainfall in the region. They distributed sweets during the farmers grievance redress meeting held at the Dindigul Collectorate on Friday. At the meeting presided over by Dindigul Collector Durgamoorthi, the farmers said residents of Kalanjipatti and Veriyappur were affected by the stone quarry operations. They demanded that the licence should be cancelled. A section of farmers complained that sewage had accumulated in a pond at Avilipatti. They also complained that the inlet channel leading to the Thattankulam tank and the supply channel leading to the Nagayakottai tank had been encroached upon. The Collector said steps would be taken to provide proper drainage facilities in Avilipatti and the encroachments would be removed. Collector Durgamoorthi presiding over the farmers redressal meeting held at Dindigul Collectorate on Friday. | Photo Credit: KARTHIKEYAN G Farmers said coconut trees in Guziliamparai area had withered and dried up. They urged the authorities to conduct a survey and provide adequate compensation to the farmers. A section of farmers demanded that a survey be conducted across the district and adequate compensation be paid to affected farmers. The Collector assured the farmers that steps would be taken to conduct a survey in this regard. Farmers complained that the road from Natham to the foothills of Sirumalai was severely damaged. Though several petitions were submitted in this regard, no action taken by the authorities. Farmers who surrendered their lands for the bypass road project should be compensated properly, they said. The Collector said steps would be taken to ensure that the road repair work was carried out expeditiously and proper compensation would be provided to the farmers. Pu

Ravi Singh, Railways’ hard-hitting willow-wielder, is quite new to the rigours of First Class cricket. The 25-year-old — who has a penchant for striking big in the shorter formats — hasn’t taken long to adjust to the longest discipline, averaging a creditable 58.2 after seven Ranji Trophy innings. Ravi, who works as a ticket collector in Howrah, had to bide his time before finding his place in the Railways team. He shifted from Varanasi to Lucknow to hone his skills under coach Saurabh Dubey, though he couldn’t quite break into the senior Uttar Pradesh set-up. But once he landed a Railways job, Ravi’s career finally stoked some steam. “After playing well for the under-23 side, I was called to the National Cricket Academy [now Centre of Excellence]. The Syed Mushtaq Ali and Vijay Hazare tournaments went quite well for me. Some of those matches were broadcast and the selectors at a higher level watched them. I was called for IPL trials, and, after seven or eight years of not playing anything [significant], things suddenly started falling my way,” Ravi said at the MAC Stadium on Saturday, two days ahead of the Ranji game against Tamil Nadu. Ravi was picked up by Rajasthan Royals for ₹95 lakh in the IPL 2026 auction. Credit: Facebook/CPI(M) West Bengal The book stalls affiliated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist) witnessed record sales in West Bengal during Durga Puja. They sold books worth over ₹1 crore even as many of their stalls faced repeated attacks. The CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, SUCI (Communist), and other Left parties have a decades-old tradition of setting up book stalls during the Durga Puja festivities. “The people have shown immense resistance against the hooliganism and attacks on the book stalls. He added that Bengal’s core reading culture cannot be changed through attacks. On October 17, one of the biggest CPI(M) book stalls in south Kolkata’s Jadavpur came under attack when a bulldozer tried to raze it. Left leaders and citizens stood in front of the bulldozer and forced it to retreat. The book stalls affiliated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist) witnessed record sales in West Bengal. 60c7acc8f1679844.title: 480 high definition cameras to be installed for Thevar Jayanthi; 18,000 police personnel to be on duty across four southern districts; DGP reviews security arrangements at Pasumpon
60c7acc8f1679844.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:14 pm IST - RAMANATHAPURAM Director General of Police and Head of Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal along with Ramanathapuram SP G. Chandeesh and other officials at the Muthuramalinga Thevar memorial ahead of Thevar Jayanthi in Ramanathapuram on Saturday. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement A total of 480 high-definition cameras, mobile CCTV cameras and specialised drones would be deployed for real-time monitoring in and around Pasumpon in Ramanathapuram district through a Centralised Control Room. The Director General of Police (Head of Police Force) Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, who visited the Pasumpon village on Saturday, took stock of the preparedness of the police force for the Thevar Jayanthi scheduled to be held on October 30. According to a press release, the camera systems are equipped with facial recognition and number plate recognition capabilities to strengthen surveillance and facilitate the timely identification of persons and vehicles, wherever required. Over 460 police patrol vehicles and quick reaction teams ( QRTs ) would be deployed for bandobust duties during the Jayanthi. The DGP inspected the commemoration venue, reviewed the preparations and interacted with the organisers to assess the arrangements and discussed operational requirements. Later, a review meeting was held at Kamuthi in which ADGP (Law and Order) T. S. Anbu Tamil Nadu, Inspector General of Police, (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari, Commissioner of Police, Madurai City, S. Rajendiran, DIGs of Police, Abhinav Kumar (Madurai Range) and Manivannan (Ramanathapuram Range) and Superintendents of Police G. Chandeesh (Ramanathapuram), Abishek Gupta (Sivaganga), Gautam Goyal (Virudhunagar), R. Shivaprasad (Thoothukudi) and Devanathan (Madurai) attended. The security would comprise seven DIGs of Police, 40 SPs and over 18,000 police

f5ed28e5f787aba0.title: APEPDCL puts 12 coastal districts on high alert for Cyclone Arnab
f5ed28e5f787aba0.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:15 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) Chairman and Managing Director Immadi Prudhvitej on Saturday (October 24, 2026) instructed field officials across 12 coastal districts to maintain maximum operational readiness following IMD warnings of ‘Cyclone Arnab’ expected between October 26 and 28. Chairing a teleconference with Superintending Engineers and Executive Engineers, the CMD ordered division-wise control rooms to be set up in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Kakinada, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, West Godavari, Eluru, and Polavaram. To ensure uninterrupted power supply to critical services, field teams have been mobilised with emergency vehicles, replacement transformers, electric poles, and clearing equipment for immediate damage restoration. The distribution utility’s corporate headquarters will monitor grid stability around the clock. Consumers have been cautioned to avoid fallen electrical wires, damaged poles, and uprooted trees, and to report power disruptions through the toll-free helpline 1912 or district control rooms. a7b5a5be05d9f25f.title: TDB to set up food safety laboratory at Pampa for evaluation of FSSAI parameters in production of prasadam
a7b5a5be05d9f25f.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 08:22 pm IST - KOCHI The Travancore Devaswom Board recently informed the Kerala High Court that a laboratory would be set up at Pampa for evaluation of prasadam as per Food Safety and Standards Authority of India parameters, including testing for pesticides and toxin levels, before the start of Sabarimala pilgrimage season. The Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar was informed that the Food Safety department would identify requirements and prepare a time-bound implementation plan. A decision was also taken to obtain National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories accreditation simultaneously, the Board stated. Currently, the samples are sent to a laboratory in Thiruvananthapuram for evaluation. The Food Safety department had apprised the Board that the equipment for the laboratory would cost around ₹2 crore to ₹3 crore and the laboratory would require an air-conditioned space of about 1000 sq. ft.; these requirements were affirmed by the Board. The department also agreed to arrange qualified personnel to operate the equipment and conduct the tests. It would examine the possibility of deploying two existing, duly appointed food safety officers for statutory inspection and sampling at Sabarimala. The Food Safety department had apprised the Board that the equipment for the laboratory would cost around ₹2 crore to ₹3 crore and the laboratory would require an air-conditioned space of about 1000 sq. ft.; these requirements were affirmed by the Board. The department also agreed to arrange qualified personnel to operate the equipment and conduct the tests. It would examine the possibility of deploying two existing, duly appointed food safety officers for statutory inspection and sampling at Sabarimala. The deceased has been identified as Ranjit Kumar Sahu, who worked as a cook at a paying guest accommodation in BTM Layout. While they were crossing the road, a white compact sedan car allegedly approached at high speed. When Ranjit and his friends signalled the driver to slow down, the occupants of the car reportedly became angry, took a U-turn and returned to confront them, the complaint stated. The occupants of the car then allegedly attempted to run the vehicle into the group. While the others managed to move aside, Ranjit was hit by the car. The car allegedly ran over his legs and dragged him for nearly 100 metres before the occupants abandoned him in the middle of the Hosur service road and fled the scene, according to the complaint. Published - October 24, 2026 07:56 pm IST Union Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh. File | Photo Credit: PTI The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has extended the tenure of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh by one year, until October 31, 2027. Also read | Defence Secretary holds key meetings at Shangri-La Dialogue 2026, pushes for Indo-Pacific security cooperation His current tenure was scheduled to end on October 31, 2026. Mr. Singh will now serve in the role until October 31, 2027, or until further orders, whichever comes first, in relaxation of FR 65(d) and Rule 16 (1A) of the All India Service (Death-Cum-Retirement Benefits) Rules, 1958, the Centre said on Saturday (October 24, 2026). Mr. Singh took over as Defence Secretary at South Block on November 1, 2024 . He took over from Giridhar Aramane, a 1988-batch IAS officer of Andhra Pradesh cadre, who had retired from service October 31, 2024 after a two year stint. He is a 1989-batch IAS officer from the Kerala cadre and assumed the charge of the Officer on Special Duty (Defence Secretary-designate) on August 20, 2024. Biju rejected a request to retrospectively approve the lease, which was executed in 2017 without the prior sanction required under Section 29 of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951. The order said the president of Ramanathapuram Grama Devaswom Society, which executed the lease, had failed to establish his legal authority to lease the property belonging to Ramanathapuram Devaswom. The society’s registration under the Societies Registration Act in 2022 did not confer the powers of a trustee under the HR&CE Act. The lease was granted to Club-6 for 30 years. The society’s president later sought retrospective approval, arguing that the arrangement was intended to generate income for the temple. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - HYDERABAD Senior BJP leader Gudur Narayana Reddy on Saturday proposed a three-point action plan to help Telangana address water, agricultural and power challenges arising from El Niño conditions, stressing the need for coordination among the government, experts, farmers and local communities. Mr. Reddy said the government’s focus on safeguarding drinking water supplies and preparing for difficult conditions in the coming months was appropriate. He said the emphasis should now be on translating policy directions into localised, measurable and publicly accessible action. He proposed setting up a small, time-bound technical cell comprising officials from the Irrigation, Groundwater and Agriculture departments, along with independent hydrologists and agronomists from agricultural universities, research institutions and ICAR institutes to coordinate measures and address emerging challenges. His second suggestion was to expedite community-level groundwater recharge and water conservation works in the most water-stressed mandals. Desilting tanks and check dams, developing farm ponds and creating percolation pits should be prioritised before peak summer, he said. As a third measure, Mr. Reddy proposed a public monitoring dashboard that tracks three key indicators: reservoir releases, the movement of drinking water tankers, and the number of hours of electricity supply to agricultural feeders. He proposed setting up a small, time-bound technical cell comprising officials from the Irrigation, Groundwater and Agriculture departments, along with independent hydrologists and agronomists from agricultural universities, research institutions and ICAR institutes to coordinate measures and address emerging challenges. His second suggestion was to expedite community-level groundwater recharge and water conservation works in the most water-stressed mandals. Desilting tanks and check dams, developing farm ponds and creating percolation pits should be prioritised before peak summer, he said. As a third measure, Mr. Reddy proposed a public monitoring dashboard that tracks three key indicators: reservoir releases, the movement of drinking water tankers, and the number of hours of electricity supply to agricultural feeders. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:36 pm IST - CHENNAI: Gursimran Singh firing in Punjab National Bank’s second goal against Karnataka on Saturday. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Hockey Karnataka fought back from a two-goal deficit to hold Punjab National Bank (PNB) to a 2-2 draw in a Pool-A match of the 97th All-India MCC-Murugappa Gold Cup hockey tournament at the SDAT Mayor Radhakrishnan Stadium here on Saturday. PNB dominated with its raids in the first half, but Karnataka showed greater purpose after the break to claw its way back into the contest. Neeraj put PNB ahead in the 14th minute with an impressive individual effort. Winning the ball from an opponent near the left sideline, he beat and dribbled past two Karnataka players and closed in on goal before slotting the ball past goalkeeper K.K. Tharun Ganapathy. Gursimran Singh doubled PNB’s lead in the 16th minute, converting a penalty corner with a drag-flick. Though Tharun intercepted the effort, he could not keep it out. Karnataka began its recovery in the 32nd minute through a well-coordinated move. Maji Ganesh found Bhrath Mahalingappa Kurtakot, who directed the ball for C.J. Rahul to finish. G. Vishwas completed Karnataka’s comeback in the 52nd minute. The side had chances to snatch victory, winning two penalty corners in the final three minutes, but failed to convert either. The results: Pool-A: Punjab National Bank 2 (Neeraj 14, Gursimran Singh 16-pc) drew with Hockey Karnataka 2 (C.J. Rahul 32, G. Vishwas 52). Pool-B: Indian Navy 5 (Rajat Sharma 15, Ashis Topno 35-pc, Nitesh 38, Sundra Pandi 58, K. Selvaraj 60) bt SAI-NCOE Bhopal 2 (Mohammed Zaid Khan 26, Bhrat Kaushik 59). Updated - October 24, 2026 07:40 pm IST - TIRUCHI The National Platform for Domestic Workers (NPDW) has urged the government to regulate the domestic service sector and provide better working conditions for its employees. At a press meet held here on Saturday, P. Clarammal, State coordinator, Tamil Nadu Domestic Workers Association, said that women formed a large section of the household service sector and they often had to work in unsafe conditions. “We urge the government to formulate laws that will ensure the personal safety of domestic workers and prevent exploitation by employers,” she said. The body focused on the enactment of comprehensive central legislation for domestic workers, and the ratification of the International Labour Organisation’s C.189 (Decent Work for Domestic Workers) convention by the Union government. The inclusion of domestic workers in the draft labour legislation proposed by the Union government in 2020 was also mooted. The body also urged the constitution of a trilateral labour board in every State to settle issues faced by the sector. Domestic workers should also be able to enrol in schemes such as the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) and Provident Fund, and a minimum salary of ₹5,000 should be made mandatory for them, it said and suggested paid leave of three months for those availing maternity and ESI leave. The KFDC has opened a Kurinji trek for enthusiasts to relish the spectacular sight. Meeshapulimala, one of the Munnar region’s highest peaks, is witnessing the blooming of Neelakurinji and will open to tourists starting Monday (October 26). The peak falls under the jurisdiction of the Kerala Forest Development Corporation (KFDC) in Munnar. KFDC Munnar Manager Akhil Das said visitors will have the opportunity to view the blooms at higher elevations. “The KFDC has arranged multi-utility vehicles (MUVs) for the 30-kilometre journey from Munnar to Meeshapulimala at a fare of ₹1,250 per person. Tourists will be picked up from the Munnar KFDC office and transported in these specially arranged vehicles. The package includes a snack box and drinking water,” he said. KFDC District Manager Sujith P.K. stated that the corporation, in association with the Wildlife Trust of India (WTI), has launched the ‘Kurinji’ mobile application for online bookings. Visitors can reserve slots and make payments directly through the app. “The key attraction at Meeshapulimala is the Neelakurinji bloom alongside sightings of the endangered Nilgiri tahr. KFDC plans to provide a unique ecotourism experience here,” Mr. Sujith said. Officials added that the Kurinji mobile app lets users easily find locations and other travel details. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:41 pm IST - KOCHI Image for representational purpose After grappling with a rise in influenza cases for months, Ernakulam has reported relatively fewer cases in October. According to the health authorities, influenza activity may be declining even as the district braces for monsoon-related diseases such as dengue and leptospirosis. A health official said the dip in influenza cases was expected. “Influenza is a seasonal outbreak, and the disease is in the declining phase now. But with intermittent rains, we are expecting an increase in dengue cases. We have to intensify precautionary measures against dengue and other monsoon-related communicable diseases. This can be done by focussing on source-reduction activities, which need to be strengthened,” the official said. A total of 335 influenza cases were reported until October 23, according to the Health department. The district registered a total of 588 dengue cases during the month, including 168 confirmed and 420 suspected cases. It also reported 31 cases of leptospirosis, including 24 confirmed and seven suspected cases, and two deaths due to the disease. Dr. Rajeev Jayadevan, convener of the research cell of the Indian Medical Association (Kerala Chapter), said influenza follows a seasonal pattern and fewer cases are likely to be reported during the current northeast monsoon season. “One of the reasons is that many people would have recently acquired immunity against the influenza virus currently in circulation. This results in a baseline level of immunity in the succeeding months, which thereafter wanes until the next wave hits,” he said. A total of 212 Domestic Breeding Checkers (DBC) have been engaged in door-to-door inspections across 60 wards of the corporation to identify mosquito larvae in water storage tanks, drums, flower pots, coconut shells, discarded tyres and other potential breeding sites. Larvicides are being applied and mosquito control activities are being carried out to prevent mosquito breeding. In addition to routine cleaning activities, intensive cleaning operations are being undertaken on a war footing to remove stagnant rainwater, garbage and other potential mosquito breeding sources from vacant plots, open spaces, parks and public spaces within the corporation limits. Fogging operations are also being carried out across all wards using four vehicle mounted fogging machines and 20 handheld pulse fogging machines to control mosquito population. Areas reporting a higher incidence of fever are being identified and special medical camps are being organised in these locations to provide fever screening and necessary medical treatment to the public. In addition to routine cleaning activities, intensive cleaning operations are being undertaken on a war footing to remove stagnant rainwater, garbage and other potential mosquito breeding sources from vacant plots, open spaces, parks and public spaces within the corporation limits. Fogging operations are also being carried out across all wards using four vehicle mounted fogging machines and 20 handheld pulse fogging machines to control mosquito population. Areas reporting a higher incidence of fever are being identified and special medical camps are being organised in these locations to provide fever screening and necessary medical treatment to the public. Published - October 24, 2026 07:29 pm IST - SIVAGANAGA In view of upcoming memorial observances, District Collector P. Akash has announced holidays for schools and colleges across seven unions in the Sivaganga district on October 27 and 30, alongside temporary closures for the district’s prominent archaeological site. The closure on October 27 marks the memorial day of Marudu Pandiyar brothers, which is observed in Kalaiyarkovil. Following this, schools and colleges will shut down again on October 30 for the birth anniversary and memorial day of freedom fighter and leader Muthuramalinga Thevar, a major annual event held at Pasumpon in the neighbouring Ramanathapuram district. The holiday directives apply to all schools and colleges situated within seven designated unions: Sivaganga, Devakottai, Tirupattur, Thiruppuvanam, Manamadurai, Kalaiyarkovil, and Ilayangudi. Additionally, as part of the safety and crowd management measures surrounding the Pasumpon Thevar Jayanthi celebrations, the district administration has announced a two-day closure for the Keeladi Site Museum in Sivaganga district, which will stay shut for visitors on October 29 and 30. Published - October 24, 2026 07:47 pm IST - MANGALURU Officials raided Kudpi's Foods located near Kadri Manjunatha Temple in the city on Saturday. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Food safety officials raided ‘Kudpi’s Foods’ located near the Kadri Manjunatha Temple in the city on Saturday and seized and sealed food products found in an unhygienic condition. A notice was issued to the unit due to lack of hygiene, an official release said. Halwa and date-based products were seized, sealed, and sent for laboratory testing, it said. The establishment was instructed to implement all measures when preparing food products, especially those intended for the festive season. It was directed to take appropriate steps to prevent risk of food poisoning, repair the drainage system, and ensure that pests, cockroaches, and rats cannot enter the production unit. Praveen Kumar, district designated officer for food safety, acting under the instructions of Health and Familay Welfare Minister U. T. Khader, the release added. Hariprasad addressing the media during his visit to Shivamogga on Saturday. | Photo Credit: S.K. Dinesh Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president B.K. Hariprasad on Saturday challenged the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to declare Nathuram Godse, who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi, as Independent India’s first terrorist. Speaking to reporters in Shivamogga, Mr. Hariprasad alleged that the BJP-led government at the Centre was trying to erase the memory of Mahatma Gandhi and his role in the freedom struggle. “Will the BJP leaders clarify their stand on Gandhi’s principles and show the courage to declare Nathuram Godse the first terrorist of Independent India?” he asked. Mr. Hariprasad also stressed the need to preserve places associated with Mahatma Gandhi during the freedom movement and to popularise his writings and speeches. He said farmers’ movements, including the Kagodu Satyagraha, should be introduced to younger generations. The KPCC president said the Congress would continue its awareness campaign against what he described as attempts by the BJP to weaken the democratic system. District Congress Committee president H.C. Yogesh, School Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa, Rajya Sabha member Naseer Hussain and others were present. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:10 pm IST - MYSURU A new book titled ‘Who are the Kodavas (Coorgs)?’ written by journalist and author P.T. Bopanna has been launched. A statement by the author said the book, which decodes the mystery of the origin of the Kodavas, is based on the first genetic study of the community. The credit for providing these early scientific leads to the puzzle should go to Coorg-born Professor Buttiyanda Kuttapa Thelma, widely known as B.K. Thelma, whose team comprised scientists from the University of Delhi South Campus and the Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad, the statement said. “The genetic study of Kodavas has not only attempted to resolve the question around the origin of Kodavas, but has also thrown insight into Indian population genetics, demonstrating that even small, tight-knit communities may harbour vast genetic complexities, shaped by centuries of migration, isolation and social customs,” the statement added. This is senior journalist Bopanna’s twelfth book. For more details, contact 9342430141. Published - October 24, 2026 07:09 pm IST Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:04 pm IST - PARVATIPURAM Telugu Desam Party MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra on Saturday (October 24, 2026) said that Parvatipuram municipality has been witnessing rapid growth as the State government has sanctioned around ₹162 crore for the development of the civic body, which was established in 1959 and is one of the oldest in the State. Along with TDP leader and his wife, Bonela Anusha, he campaigned for TDP’s candidate for the chairperson post, Belagam Karuna, and for councillors in 36 wards. Speaking to the media, he said that voters are keen to vote for the TDP, JSP, and BJP in the ensuing elections, as the government has taken steps to lay new pipelines from the Thotapalli reservoir to the city, since the old pipes were damaged long ago. He stated that the government has been spending around ₹89 crore on new pipelines and has ensured dedicated water supply to every household in Parvatipuram. Ms. Anusha said there was an overwhelming response from voters to the quick developmental activities in nook and corner of the town. She alleged that the YSRCP government had neglected the town’s development during its tenure. She added that the TDP women’s wing formed special teams to intensify a door-to-door campaign in the next few days. Rajagopal Asian Brown Flycatcher | Photo Credit: V. Rajagopal Yellow Wagtail spotted in Tiruchi. | Photo Credit: V. Rajagopal Birdwatching enthusiasts in and around Tiruchi have reported a steady inflow of migratory birds from late September to the region, with their flight schedules possibly affected by the absence of summer rain and the ongoing northeast monsoon in Tamil Nadu this year. “Due to the prolonged hot weather this year, fewer migratory birds were spotted near Tiruchi’s water bodies in late September compared to 2025. We noticed the Asian Brown Flycatcher and the Brownbreasted Flycatcher near Kulumayi Amman Temple, and the Common Sandpiper at Koothappar Big Tank in Tiruchi. Yellow Wagtail, which breeds in Europe and Asia, was spotted near Musiri and Kiliyur in recent weeks. However, we expect more avian migration over the coming weeks as the winter monsoon sets in,” V. Rajagopal, a local birdwatcher, told The Hindu. E-Bird India, an online collaborative project managed by Bird Count India, lists five new species spotted in Tiruchi region by birdwatchers. 8c611d615f5121fb.title: K. Annamalai unhappy over politics of seeking votes by promising freebies in Karnataka
8c611d615f5121fb.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:23 pm IST - MANGALURU Former IPS officer K. Annamalai speaking at a programme in Udupi on Saturday. | Photo Credit: UMESH S. SHETTIGAR Former IPS officer and founder of ‘We The Leaders’ K. Annamalai said on Saturday that politics in Karnataka needs to become more responsible than limiting to a style of politics that seeks votes by promising freebies. Speaking at the State-level retailers’ convention of the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) in Udupi, Mr. Annamalai said that political parties should focus on providing good governance to the State. Karnataka deserves better governance. It is not enough for development to be concentrated solely in Bengaluru, he said. “Karnataka should not remain a State dependent solely on Bengaluru, but rather achieve development across all its regions,” he said. Mr. Annamalai said that a change in the political system is possible only when competition between political parties is based on developmental projects. The government’s achievements should serve as the benchmark for political rivalry. Such a responsible and competitive political system can lead to improvements in governance, he said. Mr. Annamalai said that politics should not be limited merely to a “poster culture”. Instead of putting up posters announcing the arrival of a Chief Minister or a former Chief Minister, there should be posters that inform the public about the contributions the government. Mr. Annamalai said that a change in the political system is possible only when competition between political parties is based on developmental projects. The government’s achievements should serve as the benchmark for political rivalry. Such a responsible and competitive political system can lead to improvements in governance, he said. Mr. Annamalai said that politics should not be limited merely to a “poster culture”. Instead of putting up posters announcing the arrival of a Chief Minister or a former Chief Minister, there should be posters that inform the public about the contributions the government.
