MOORTHY The current spell of rain over the past few days has battered many key roads in the city, causing hardship to commuters and motorists. Since the onset of the northeast monsoon on October 15, Tiruchi has been getting rainfall. The rainfall was not heavy in the city up to Thursday and it received only light showers. However, it received heavy rain in different parts on Friday.The continuous rainfall has damaged many arterial roads and interior roads. Uneven road surfaces and potholes have become common sights on major stretches, with the top layer eroded in many places. The damaged patches have led to frequent skidding incidents, particularly affecting two-wheeler riders. Anna Nagar roads, Karur bypass, old Madurai road, West Boulevard Road, Major Saravanan Road and important stretches around the Central Bus Stand, such as Rockins Road, McDonalds Road, VOC Road, and Williams Road, have suffered significant deterioration. With heavy vehicle movement continuing through these roads, the loose surface material has begun to dislodge, worsening driving conditions. Recently patched up roads too have also suffered the damage. a7a625e6948fe0cc.title: TN coach Murray wants the players to develop a cohesive style of play
a7a625e6948fe0cc.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 07:18 pm IST - CHENNAI William Murray. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU William Murray, Hockey Unit of Tamil Nadu’s (HUTN) high-performance coach, wants the State team to be more than just a winning unit. The Englishman, who joined the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT) in May on a two-year contract, wants his players to develop an exciting, cohesive style of hockey that draws crowds. An FIH coach educator, Murray first came to India this year to conduct Level 3 coaching courses for Hockey India (HI) in Rourkela and Hyderabad before taking up the role of coaching the Tamil Nadu men’s team. He has worked in Hong Kong and Belgium, and coached England’s u-18 and Scotland’s u-21 teams. Murray believes the lack of early exposure to artificial turf has influenced Indian players’ technical and tactical development. “Too often, it’s very individualised here. Even things like pushing (push pass), since it’s not done in the same way on gravel, grass, or dirt pitches, there’s a desire to get the ball off the floor as much as possible. Whereas on astro, you want the ball on the floor, where it moves quickly but smoothly. That allows the whole team to stay connected up the pitch and work together. “I’m trying to implement some quite rigorous tactical concepts, which will take time. I want us to be exciting - to play fast, with style and swagger, but also in a connected way,” he said. The coach is also keen to strengthen the State’s hockey pipeline. “More than just focusing on one team, for me it’s about making sure the whole ecosystem is rich, so that any young player, whatever their background, if they’re good enough, gets the opportunity and understanding to be nurtured and grow to their potential,” he said. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:08 pm IST - Hyderabad Researchers found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some Konkani-speaking communities, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. | Photo Credit: Jaison Sequeira Ancient migrations into South Asia may have involved women as well as men, according to a new genetic study of Konkani-speaking communities along India’s west coast. Comparisons with ancient DNA suggested that prehistoric migrations into South Asia were more complex than previously understood. Researchers from the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, and Mangalore University found traces of West Eurasian and Steppe-linked maternal lineages among some groups, offering fresh insights into the region’s complex population history. The findings of the study led by CCMB’s K. Thangaraj and Mangalore University's M.S. Mustak challenge the notion that Bronze Age migrations into the subcontinent were driven predominantly by males. The Konkan region, stretching from Daman in the north to the Gangavalli River and Karwar in the south, is known for its rich cultural, linguistic and social diversity. Although Konkani is spoken across the region, its speakers belong to several communities with distinct histories and traditions. To trace their maternal origins, researchers analysed maternally inherited mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) from 295 Konkani-speaking individuals. The population was broadly classified into Sarasvata and non-Sarasvata groups, based on oral traditions regarding ancestry linked to the ancient Sarasvati region. Updated - October 24, 2026 07:15 pm IST - COIMBATORE During the National Management Week 2026, around 250 students of PSG Institute of Management (PSGIM), Coimbatore, will take management learning beyond the classroom and into the community through initiatives focusing on waste management, rabies awareness, and preventing pollution caused by indiscriminate poster pasting, under the overarching theme of ‘Clean and Safe City’. Observed from October 26 to 31 under the aegis of the Association of Indian Management Schools (AIMS-New Delhi), the initiatives reflect a simple yet meaningful belief: building a better city is a shared responsibility. During the week, students will engage with communities at more than 30 identified waste hotspots across Coimbatore. By promoting waste segregation at source and responsible disposal, they will encourage everyday practices that protect the environment and improve neighbourhoods for everyone. The initiative will also highlight the connection between unmanaged waste and street dogs. Discarded food and other waste can attract dogs to public spaces, increase the risk of conflict and create unhealthy conditions for people and animals. Students will also conduct rabies awareness activities across 30 identified locations in the city in association with the Humane Animal Society (HAS), to promote rabies prevention, safe interactions with street dogs and humane animal care. These activities will reinforce the importance of keeping public spaces free of food waste and other refuse that can attract dogs. 40b7e4fba524fcb4.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Published - October 24, 2026 04:41 pm IST - MUMBAI A man walks past the Kotak Mahindra Bank branch in New Delhi | Photo Credit: Reuters Kotak Mahindra Bank reported a 26% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to ₹5,645.38 crore for the quarter ended September, beating analysts’ estimates based on LSEG data but falling short of domestic brokerages’ projections of 27-32% growth. The lender’s total income rose 18% YoY to ₹29,426.88 crore. Other income increased nearly 25% to ₹9,571.01 crore. However, sequentially, total income and other income declined 2.1% and 18.3%, respectively. Net interest income (NII) grew 16% YoY to ₹8,459 crore. Net interest margin (NIM), however, contracted to 4.31% from 4.54% in the preceding quarter. The bank attributed the decline to deposits mobilised under the Reserve Bank of India’s special window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) accounts, through which it raised ₹55,344 crore. Asset quality improved, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.04% from 1.39% a year earlier. Net NPA fell to 0.24% from 0.32%. Provisions declined 15% YoY to ₹803 crore. Operating expenses rose 14% YoY to ₹5,271 crore, partly offsetting the gains from higher income and lower provisions. For the first half of FY27, net profit stood at ₹11,125.84 crore. As of September 30, net advances grew 25% YoY to ₹5,77,295 crore, while deposits increased 23% to ₹6,51,491 crore. The 31-year-old Indian, who won the Japan Open Super 750 in July, displayed immaculate temperament to register a 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 win over world No. 22 Akechi in an hour and 13 minutes. bcfc461a8cec3809.title: Air pollution alert: 3 Punjab cities among world's top 10 most polluted; Check AQI
bcfc461a8cec3809.summary: Amritsar, Bathinda and Faridkot in Punjab were among the five most polluted cities in India, according to real-time Air Quality Index (AQI) rankings. Amritsar recorded an AQI of 392, followed by Bathinda at 368 and Faridkot at 360. Meerut in Uttar Pradesh and Fatehpur rounded out the top five, with AQI readings of 355 and 354, respectively. Meanwhile, Delhi continued to record ‘poor’ air quality on Friday, with an AQI of 230. The capital’s air quality is expected to remain in the ‘poor’ category over the next nine days, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System. These rankings are time-sensitive and can change as pollution levels and weather conditions fluctuate. Delhi recorded an AQI of 230 on Friday, placing it in the ‘poor’ category. According to data from the Central Pollution Control Board ’s (CPCB) Sameer app, three of the capital’s 56 monitoring stations recorded ‘very poor’ air quality. Pusa recorded the highest AQI among the monitoring stations, at 324. Meanwhile, 36 stations reported ‘poor’ air quality, while the remaining 17 recorded ‘moderate’ conditions. The Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that Delhi’s air quality will remain ‘poor’ from October 23 to October 26 and is likely to stay in the same category for the following six days. Weather conditions are expected to remain unfavourable for the dispersal of pollutants. According to the forecast, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, combined with an average wind speed of less than 10 kmph, can hinder the dispersion of pollutants. Such conditions can allow pollutants to accumulate near the surface, prolonging periods of poor air quality. According to the Decision Support System for Air Quality Management in Delhi, developed by IITM Pune, the transport sector accounted for 20.3% of the capital’s air pollution. Other identified sources included: The data also showed that neighbouring National Capital Region (NCR) districts contributed to Delhi’s pollution. Gurugram

beb21fd12844965c.title: Kumaran Nagar bus terminus in Kolathur needs sprucing up
beb21fd12844965c.summary: You don’t have any Active Subscription. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Additional Subscription Benefits Need help with your subscription? Updated - October 24, 2026 05:20 pm IST Kumaran Nagar bus terminus on October 20, 2026. This has turned the terminus slippery and flyblown, and it smells bad. Kumaran Nagar bus terminus in Kolathur is unhygienic with cow dung all over the place. Commuters say that the bus services operated from the terminus are very poor, and hence the terminus remains vacant for most of the day; also, commuters hardly wait here for the buses. So, all these have provided a conducive environment for cows to occupy the terminus. Alcohol bottles found at the terminus point to misuse of the terminus for consumption. It may be noted this terminus was redeveloped and inaugurated early this year but the facility fell into a state of neglect within a few weeks. The toilets are also unhygienic due to the erratic water supply. The room meant for lactating mothers is kept under lock-and-key. Further, there is no timekeeper here. Commuters are clueless when the next bus would arrive. Though there is a room dedicated for the timekeeper, it also remains locked. Services operated from the terminus need to be improved. There are buses only to Guindy and Anna Square. Further, the frequency is also very poor and not reliable. So commuters rely on share autorickshaws to access Paper Mills Road. From there, they go to the Retteri junction or the Perambur bus terminus or the Thiru Vi Ka Nagar terminus to access buses to other places. This is quite inconvenient. Where is the need to redevelop a bus terminus which receives poor patronage? N. 4d68a1f200d353d5.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2FY27 result: Net profit jumps 53% to ₹858 crore
4d68a1f200d353d5.summary: AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday reported a 53 per cent surge in net profit at Rs 858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income. The lender had earned a net profit of Rs 561 crore in the year-ago period. Total income rose to Rs 6,382 crore in the quarter under review from Rs 5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing. Interest income increased to Rs 5,612 crore as against Rs 4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year. Net interest income of the bank improved to Rs 2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent. Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025. Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026

7851e78b35628447.title: India's forex reserves decline $5 billion to $721 billion: RBI data
7851e78b35628447.summary: India's forex reserves dropped by USD 5.011 billion to USD 721.016 billion during the week ended October 16, the Reserve Bank of India said on Friday. In the previous reporting week, the kitty declined by USD 8.578 billion to USD 726.027 billion. The reserves touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion for the week ended September 4, driven by heavy greenback inflow as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record nearly USD 133 billion but have been on a declining trend ever since. Experts attribute the sharp decline in the kitty to deployment of FCNR(B) resources and currency defence put up by the RBI through dollar sales. For the week ended October 16, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 5.758 billion to USD 591.847 billion, according to the data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). ed7d9cd2c46fa5d0.summary: The government will share the cost of high-risk deepwater oil and gas exploration with energy companies under the Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan scheme, offering to pay part of the cost of risky exploration wells, fund seismic mapping of offshore basins and help build shared production facilities. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas issued operational guidelines for the Samudra Manthan programme, which aims to improve the economics of exploring India's deepwater and ultra-deepwater basins, where high drilling costs and uncertain geological prospects have constrained investment. The scheme aims to cut India's heavy reliance on imported hydrocarbons. The guidelines say it will run through FY2030-31, with FY2026-27 as a preparatory year and spending in FY2027-28 to FY2030-31 as Phase I. 1df76ae7afa31607.title: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Q2 profit jumps 44% to ₹409 crore
1df76ae7afa31607.summary: CG Power and Industrial Solutions on Friday posted 44 per cent jump in consolidated net profit at Rs 409.09 crore for September quarter FY27, supported by higher revenues. The Mumbai-headquartered entity had clocked a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 284.44 crore in the year-ago period, it said in an exchange filing. During the quarter, the company's total income increased to Rs 3,883.25 crore from Rs 2,988.89 crore in Q2 FY26. From power systems segment, the revenue was Rs 1,766.76 crore as against Rs 1,254.49 crore in the year-ago quarter. The industrial systems business contributed a revenue of Rs 1,868.61 crore in the quarter as against Rs 1,533.33 crore in July-September FY26. The company's board approved enhancing capex investment for the GIS brownfield project at Vilholi, Nashik, from Rs 35.17 crore to Rs 44.62 crore. It also gave nod to invest Rs 15.31 crore to enhance EHV (extra high voltage) circuit breaker manufacturing capacity by 3,600 units (annually) at S3 Unit-II ...

0404e1873c16f985.title: Petronet LNG, Gruner Renewable float JV to develop compressed biogas plants
0404e1873c16f985.summary: Petronet LNG and Gruner Renewable Energy have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop a portfolio of compressed biogas (CBG) plants across India, which entails an initial investment of about Rs 1,200 crore. This model is first of its kind in India, where the JV partner is undertaking sourcing of feedstock, EPC, operations and maintenance and offtake of organic manure, thus integrating the CBG value chain, a statement said. The proposed partnership envisages the development of 10 CBG plants, each with a designed capacity of 18 metric tonnes per day, taking the planned aggregate capacity to approximately 180 metric tonnes per day. The combined investment for the proposed portfolio is estimated at around Rs 1,200 crore, it informed. The partnership brings together Petronet LNG's established position in India's LNG and natural-gas infrastructure ecosystem with Gruner Renewable Energy's experience in CBG project development, engineering, feedstock mobilisation and plant operations. 791461cc61bd7ae8.title: BCGCL begins construction work on ₹25,000 crore coal gasification project
791461cc61bd7ae8.summary: Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Ltd (BCGCL), the joint venture of Coal India Ltd (CIL) and BHEL, has started ground construction activities for its Rs 25,000 crore coal gasification project in Odisha, with most of the tenders awarded, its Managing Director Peeyush Kumar said on Thursday. The development assumes significance in the wake of the country's push to build 100 million tonne of coal gasification capacity by 2030 under the National Coal Gasification Mission, aimed at converting coal into chemicals and bringing down the import dependence on products such as LNG, urea, ammonia and methanol. "We are going ahead with the joint venture of BHEL and Coal India, which is BCGCL....I am happy to share that we have started ground construction activities... Most of the tenders have been awarded and construction has started," Kumar said during the 17th Edition of Gasification India 2026 organised by Mission Energy Foundation. BCGCL--a joint venture in which CIL holds the majority

d7d7f7c06453556f.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Bank on Thursday reported a 10.6 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 546.36 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, driven by earnings growth and improvement in asset quality. The bank earned Rs 494.11 crore net profit in the year-ago period. Sequentially, its profits surged 28.8 per cent from Rs 424.18 crore in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, a bank spokesperson said. The bank announced the financial results after its Board of Directors reviewed and approved the quarterly and half-yearly figures at a meeting held at its corporate headquarters here on Thursday. Its net interest income rose 5 per cent during the quarter to Rs 1,502 crore. The lender's other income more than doubled to Rs 314.90 crore from Rs 153.76 cr a year ago. For the first half of the current fiscal year, the bank's operating expenditure grew 1.5 per cent, and its operating profit rose over 15 per cent to Rs 1,492 crore. 24c4804db1ab92fc.title: Sony India FY26 net profit rises 19% to ₹187 crore, revenue grows 0.85%
24c4804db1ab92fc.summary: Consumer electronics maker Sony India's profit rose 19 per cent to Rs 186.88 crore in FY26, while its revenue from operations grew marginally by 0.85 per cent to Rs 7,917.99 crore, according to regulatory filings. Total income, including other income, increased 1.32 per cent to Rs 8,022.73 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to financial data accessed through business intelligence platform Tofler. Sony India, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Japanese technology major Sony Corporation, had reported a profit of Rs 157.03 crore and revenue from operations of Rs 7,851.08 crore in FY25. India is Sony's fourth-largest market globally, after the US, China and Japan. The company aims to make India its third-largest market worldwide, overtaking its home market Japan. Sony India's advertising and promotional expenses declined marginally to Rs 182.58 crore in FY26 from Rs 183.71 crore a year earlier. 23929620c4ef6107.title: India must make growth employment-intensive, not just fast: Ex-RBI chief
23929620c4ef6107.summary: Sustaining economic growth of 7 per cent or more will require stronger private investment, labour-intensive manufacturing, better human capital and deeper integration into global value chains, former RBI Governor D Subbarao has said. Subbarao also said that the challenge is not merely to grow fast, but to make growth productive, employment-intensive and resilient. "India's 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter suggests that the economy is more resilient than many expected...I am optimistic about India's medium-term prospects, but not complacent," he told PTI. Recently, the World Bank raised India's GDP growth forecast for the current fiscal year to 7.1 per cent, up 0.5 percentage points from its April projections, supported by robust domestic demand and strong exports, despite global headwinds. "Sustaining growth of 7 per cent or more will require stronger private investment, labour-intensive manufacturing, better human capital and deeper integration into global value chains..

b603c52963c725a4.title: Essar Ports wins ₹2,276 crore Tuna Tekra terminal project at Kandla
b603c52963c725a4.summary: Essar Ports has secured a letter of award from Deendayal Port Authority to develop an 18.33-million-tonne-a-year multipurpose cargo terminal at Tuna Tekra in Gujarat's Kandla port, marking a renewed push by the group to expand its ports business. The project carries an estimated cost of Rs 2,276.06 crore, including an investment of Rs 1,552.57 crore by Essar Ports and Rs 723.49 crore by the port authority, the company said in a statement. The terminal will be developed under a 30-year build-operate-transfer concession through the public-private partnership route, with Essar emerging as the highest bidder in a global competitive bidding process. The project will add capacity for handling dry and other multipurpose cargo on India's western coast, as the country seeks to expand port infrastructure to accommodate growing trade and improve logistics efficiency, it said. The proposed facility will have four berths, each measuring 300 metres, providing a total berth length of 1,200 metres

Rubio, who arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday afternoon, first met Adani, followed by a meeting with Chandrasekaran, sources said. Neither side released details of the meetings. Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons, the Tata Group's holding company, oversees a sprawling business empire with interests in automobiles, .

c059d79704334d01.summary: The three-day Army Commanders' Conference began here on Wednesday, during which Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will release the 'Land Warfare Doctrine' -- a vision document providing an overarching framework to prepare the force for challenges posed by the evolving character of warfare and future conflicts. It brings together the senior leadership of the Indian Army to deliberate on the evolving security environment, operational preparedness, capability development and future-ready transformation initiatives, officials said. Chaired by the Chief of the Army Staff, Gen Dhiraj Seth, the apex-level biannual forum is being held from October 21-23, the defence ministry said. "With its comprehensive agenda, the conference will provide an important forum for the senior leadership of the Army to review ongoing initiatives, identify future thrust areas and formulate appropriate policy directions towards building a progressive, adaptive, technologically enabled and future-ready Indian Army,"

The country's GDP registered modest growth alongside an increase in per capita income in dollar terms, reflecting a sluggish pace of recovery in the country's overall output compared with the previous year, the government said. In May 2026, the government had projected the economy to grow by 3.70 pc in FY26, revising its earlier estimate of 4 pc. The downward adjustment now indicates that the country fell short of its GDP target, a Dawn report showed. The revised growth rates in agriculture, industry and services in FY26 are 3.50pc, 3.34pc and 3.81pc, respectively, compared with earlier growth rates of 2.89pc, 3.51pc and 4.09 pc. The 23-year-old from Telangana, who also holds the Asian record, is a two-time Para World Championships medallist, having won the gold in 2024. She is also a Paralympic bronze winner in the same event. On Tuesday, Japan's Niina Kanno (58.92sec) won the silver and her compatriot Akane Kato (1:00.26sec) took bronze. The T20 classification covers athletes with intellectual impairments. Athletes in this category experience challenges with processing information, concentration, and executing race plans or tactical strategies. Hailing from a remote village in Telangana's Warangal, Deepthi's parents are small farmers, who also worked as labourers in their village. 7482ead028b895f1.title: Indian table tennis players bag five bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026
7482ead028b895f1.summary: Ravi Baby Sahana and Prachi Pandey scripted history by becoming India's first para table tennis players to make the podium in the standing category at the Asian Para Games, as the country secured five bronze medals here on Tuesday. Paralympics medallist Bhavina Patel, Sonalben Patel, Prachi and Sahana all went down to accomplished Paralympic medallists in their respective women's singles semifinals, while Jehan Madan bagged a bronze medal in the men's singles class 1 event by virtue of finishing fourth in a five-paddler field. The haul also took India past its medal tally from the previous edition, where it had won two bronze medals in para table tennis. Sahana and Prachi's bronze were particularly significant as they became the first Indians to win medals in the standing category at the Asian Para Games. Tamil Nadu's Sahana went down 8-11, 2-11, 4-11 to five-time Paralympic gold medallist Mao Jingdian of China in the Class 9 semifinal. Class 9 in para table tennis is a standing .

5d3d056af94e4cda.title: India to host SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum by year-end: Rajnath Singh
5d3d056af94e4cda.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday announced that India will host the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum by the end of this year and invited all member countries to participate in it. Singh made these remarks while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. "India, at the end of this year, will host the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. We invite all SCO member countries to participate in it," Singh said. During the SCO summit of the Council of Heads of State in Tianjin in 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to create a Civilisational Dialogue Forum to strengthen people-to-people ties and allow sharing of the richness of ancient civilisations, art, literature, and traditions on a global stage. Singh also mentioned the 25-year journey of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. "At the SCO Summit in Bishkek, our leaders had highlighted the 25-year journey of the Shanghai Cooperation

129317366508a5c6.title: Shafali Verma reprimanded for breaching ICC Code of Conduct in 2nd T20I
129317366508a5c6.summary: India vice-captain Shafali Verma was on Tuesday handed an official reprimand for throwing the ball to the ground in frustration after dropping a catch during the second T20I against Zimbabwe. The 22-year-old was found to have breached Level 1 of the ICC Code of Conduct during India's nine-wicket victory in Raipur on Sunday. Verma was found to have breached Article 2.2 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to "abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during an International Match," an ICC media release said. In addition to this, one demerit point has been added to Verma's disciplinary record, for whom it was the first offence in a 24-month period. The incident occurred in the 12th over of Zimbabwe's innings when Verma, after dropping Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano at mid-off off Shree Charani's bowling, threw the ball to the ground in frustration. The group brings together a dedicated global workforce that pairs Google's full-stack, enterprise-ready AI platform with Cognizant's domain, industry and engineering expertise as an AI-builder, according to a release. Supported by more than 18,000 dedicated Cognizant associates, the new group represents a substantial joint investment and builds on the momentum created by Cognizant's dedicated Gemini practice launched in April 2026. The new group is designed to bridge the path from pilot to production, equipping enterprises with the ability to safely deploy resilient, enterprise-grade agents that can help drive measurable business value, the release said. "Establishing our dedicated Gemini Frontier Capability Group lets our best frontier engineering talent focus entirely on getting frontier AI into production

0f72b5b6c7dbe233.summary: Gianni Infantino's campaign for re-election as FIFA president is set to move this week to Japan and a meeting scheduled for Wednesday with the Asian Football Confederation. This comes after Infantino apologized last week in Zurich, Switzerland, to FIFA's 37-member ruling council - which he chairs - for "mistakes" he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2 billion sell-off plan for the World Cup. The council is the main decision-making body at FIFA with a global spread of officials. The planned meeting with Asian soccer leaders is to be held in a five-star hotel in Tokyo with the media largely excluded. ccbf19cc8b4c46a4.title: Grocery to overtake mobiles as India's online retail market to cross $90 bn
ccbf19cc8b4c46a4.summary: India's online retail market is projected to cross USD 90 billion in 2026, registering an annual growth of 22-24 per cent, its fastest expansion in five years, driven by everyday consumption categories like grocery rather than mobile phones, Redseer Strategy Consultants said in a report. According to the analysis, e-commerce gross merchandise value (GMV) expanded roughly 25 per cent year-on-year to about USD 38 billion in the first half (H1) of 2026, marking its strongest H1 performance in four years. While online retail accelerated, mobile sales remained flat at 0 per cent growth during the first half and are projected to grow by just 2-3 per cent across the full year due to sharp price increases curbing sales volumes. Consequently, the grocery segment is poised to overtake mobile phones as the second-largest category in Indian e-commerce, behind fashion. 8fb74366d3fdbad4.title: Focusing on midterms: Vance declines to endorse Netanyahu for reelection
8fb74366d3fdbad4.summary: Vice President J D Vance declined to endorse Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection a day after President Donald Trump endorsed the embattled Israeli leader. "The president has the most influential endorsement in American or international political history," Vance said on Monday during an interview with journalist Mark Halperin. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on the midterms," Vance said, while travelling to campaign for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley of North Carolina. "So, I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections." Vance has campaigned for a foreign leader -- then-Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orban -- last spring before the right-wing leader's party lost that country's parliamentary election. Vance's deference to Trump on Netanyahu comes at an extraordinarily sensitive time for Jewish Americans and the US alliance with Israel. 6dc6053bbb569952.title: Just Dial Q2 profit declines 9.73% to ₹107.8 cr despite 13% revenue growth
6dc6053bbb569952.summary: Just Dial Ltd, a leading local search engine, has reported a decline of 9.73 per cent in its consolidated net profit to Rs 107.8 crore in the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis. It had posted a net profit of Rs 119.44 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing. However, Just Dial's revenue from operations was up 13.11 per cent in the September quarter at Rs 342.82 crore, compared to Rs 303.07 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago. Just Dial's total expenses stood at Rs 262.81 crore, up 14.6 per cent YoY in the September quarter. The company, owned by Reliance Retail Ventures, the retail arm of billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Ltd, reported a 5.6 per cent rise in total income to Rs 397.38 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Share of Just Dial Ltd on Monday settled 2.82 per cent higher at Rs 732.55 apiece on the BSE.

20bf7e85d649d76c.title: PM Modi greets people on Vijayadashami, wishes happiness and prosperity
20bf7e85d649d76c.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday greeted people on the occasion of Vijayadashami and prayed that the festival would enrich everyone's life with happiness, prosperity, and success. "Heartiest greetings of Vijayadashami to everyone. May this festival of victory, filled with joy and faith, empower everyone's resolve with renewed strength," Modi said in a post on X in Hindi. "May every life be enriched with happiness, prosperity, and success-this is my sincere wish," he added. The festival celebrates Lord Rama's vanquishing the 10-headed demon king Ravana, and symbolises the triumph of good over evil. It is celebrated across the country with revellers coming out in large numbers to witness the burning of Ravana effigies, marking a culmination of 10 days of festivities filled with rituals, songs, dance and processions.

5cb2e7ba575b3eac.title: UN food agency cuts aid to Palestinians in Gaza, West Bank amid fund crunch
5cb2e7ba575b3eac.summary: The United Nations has cut food assistance to 5,00,000 Palestinians in Gaza and 2,00,000 in the West Bank due to a serious funding shortage, the head of the UN food agency said. Carl Skau, acting head of the World Food Program, on Monday urged the international community to provide USD 450 million so the agency could restore the cut assistance and provide hot meals and food parcels in Gaza and the West Bank for the next six months. Because of the money shortage, the number of people receiving assistance was reduced this month from 1.6 million to 1.1 million in Gaza and from 4,00,000 to 2,00,000 in the West Bank, he said. Skau, who had just visited both territories, told UN correspondents in a video briefing from Jerusalem that life in Gaza remains "absolutely brutal" and incredibly dangerous, with UN teams recording about 50 attacks per day in the past week. Nonetheless, he said that since last October's ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, "we have been able to push back on famine"

7219997d9a65701c.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Tuesday cautioned that regime-change agitations do not resolve fundamental problems, warning that protests could become instruments of political interests and fuel divisions in society rather than delivering solutions. Addressing the annual Vijayadashami gathering here, Bhagwat cited recent upheavals in Bangladesh, Nepal, France, and Albania, asserting that forces pursuing their own interests use regime change as a means to alter political circumstances, rarely achieving intended results. "They claim that changing a regime will change the situation, but that has never really happened," he said. Bhagwat claimed that a stronger India would constrain such forces, making the country a target of attempts to weaken and divide it. While some global powers want India to develop, they do not want it to become too powerful, as it could challenge their dominance, he added. 0e7efd4b08cd369c.summary: The finance ministry on Saturday said the legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, a Delhi High Court judgement and successive Union Budget speeches reflect the evolution of its policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank. The Cabinet earlier this week approved strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank by selling 60.72 per cent stake to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for about Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion). The deal is the largest foreign investment in India's financial sector so far and a major milestone in the country's banking privatisation drive. In a clarification on the legislative developments regarding reduction in government holding in IDBI Bank, the ministry said the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, held that the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, contained no prohibition against reducing the government's stake in IDBI Bank Ltd. "I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio said in response to a question on the waivers granted by Trump under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act or the Graham Act. On Friday, Trump waived key provisions of the Graham Act that authorised punitive tariffs on countries purchasing Russian oil, offering relief to India. a722e6aae76e6979.title: Hybrids, CNG may contribute 50% of sales in 2-3 years: Renault India CEO
a722e6aae76e6979.summary: As French carmaker Renault pushes multifuel powertrain strategy in India, Renault India CEO Stephane Deblaise said hybrid and CNG technology can possibly account for almost half of the automaker's powertrain mix in its sales over the next 2-3 years. His comments came as the company bets big on hybrid and CNG technology in its India strategy. The automaker on Saturday launched its first strong hybrid offering on the Duster SUV, and plans to launch factory-fitted CNG models in the future. When asked how Renault India's powertrain mix could look over the next 2-3 years, Deblaise told PTI: "It is possible, 50 per cent is possible from hybrid and CNG, but we do not have a target." India's car market is increasingly seeing multiple powertrain technologies develop alongside each other, including hybrids, CNG and electric vehicles, rather than one single technology replacing another immediately. Automakers see hybrid technology as a practical bridge as the electric vehicle ecosystem evolve

7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.title: Centre revises Ladakh hill council rules, allows 7-24 elected members
7df0f8c7e7e0d7b1.summary: The Centre has amended the legal terminology, administrative structure and electoral provisions governing the Autonomous Hill Development Councils in Ladakh to align them with the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which led to the creation of the Union territory of Ladakh. Under the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Amendment) Regulation, the number of elected seats in each Council will be determined by the Ladakh administration, with a minimum of seven and a maximum of 24 seats. The administration can nominate up to four members from among women and "unrepresented communities", subject to the one-sixth limit of the population, the regulation states. The sitting Lok Sabha MP representing Ladakh will be an ex-officio member of the Councils constituted for each district.
